title: Move the untriaged-findings gate from every tick to the close-out
description:
OPERATOR DECISION, 2026-09-19. The hold changes.

Today epic-ncv stopped FIVE times for nothing but untriaged findings. The rule as built means a run is unattended only if nothing finds anything — and a run that finds nothing is a run that was not looking. The Phase 4 gate counts one intervention as failure, so the hold and the gate cannot both stand.

The reasoning for the hold is still right: a finding that falls on the floor is the failure it exists to stop. What changes is WHERE it is caught. Findings now ride to the epic PR, where a person sees them at merge time — which is already what the epic acceptance allows for the FINAL REVIEW's findings, so this extends an existing rule rather than inventing one.

Work:
- A tick with untriaged findings closes; the findings are carried.
- The epic PR body lists every untriaged finding, by tick, with its severity and body — not a count, the text, because a link nobody opens is a finding on the floor.
- The close-out must refuse to hand over if a finding was filed and does NOT appear on the PR. That refusal is what replaces the hold, and it belongs at the one gate a person actually reads.
-  keeps working for triage before the merge; nothing about the durable record changes.

From pxc, finding 7b974094, which put the choice plainly rather than picking for us.
notes:
2026-09-19 15:50 - Correction: a shell-quoting slip dropped two words from the bullet above. It should read:

  - "ticfac findings" keeps working for triage before the merge; nothing about
    the durable record changes.

The durable finding record, its schema and its triage verbs are unchanged. What changes is only whether an untriaged finding STOPS the run.
2026-09-19 15:57 - 2026-09-19 — BLOCKED, and the blockers were found by the same review that prompted this tick.

4sb: internal/forge offers only Find/Open/CI. There is NO way to write to a pull request. The 'carry findings to the PR' half of this decision is not merely unbuilt, it is currently impossible.

b50: the untriaged-findings hold is the ONLY thing that currently stops a review answering NOT READY from closing and releasing the close-out — and the durable record spells that review 'ready-to-merge'.

So implementing this tick alone would remove a safety net and put nothing in its place: an epic whose own review says it is not ready would hand itself over, with a record a reader would take for approval, and no findings on the PR because nothing can write there.

Order: 4sb and b50 first, then this. The decision stands; its sequencing was wrong and the review caught it.
2026-09-19 16:15 - 2026-09-19 — REDESIGNED after the operator pointed out what I had missed.

I filed this as 'carry findings to the PR' and blocked it on the forge learning to write. That was wrong, and the reason is that findings ALREADY report outside the tick:

    .ticfac/runs/<run-id>/findings/*.json on the integration branch — 32 of them
    on epic/ncv right now — content-keyed, durable, and listable with
    'ticfac findings <epic>' without touching a tick.

So the hold preserves nothing. A finding cannot fall on the floor; it is a committed file on the branch before the tick is ever refused. What the hold actually forces is a DECISION, and it forces it at the worst possible moment — once per tick, mid-run, five times in this epic.

The fix is therefore much smaller than a PR-writing forge:

  - a tick with untriaged findings CLOSES and the run continues
  - the CLOSE-OUT refuses to hand over while any finding of the run is untriaged,
    naming them
  - that is one decision point instead of N, at the end, where a person is
    already being asked to look

The safety net is not removed, it is moved. Nothing needs the forge to write, so 4sb is unblocked from this and stands on its own as a genuine improvement rather than a prerequisite. b50 is likewise a real defect and not a blocker here.

Credit where due: I had convinced myself of a dependency that did not exist, and the operator asked the one question that dissolved it.
2026-09-19 16:27 - 2026-09-19 — pxc's third pass found the mechanism that makes this tick urgent rather than merely tidy: 80x.

A review tick held for untriaged findings is not closed after triage — it is RE-DISPATCHED. pxc ran attempts 9, 10 and 11 against byte-identical source, three full frontier reviews of one diff.

And the loop only terminates when a review reports nothing. Each re-dispatch can raise new findings, which raise a new hold. So the system pays frontier-tier money until it gets a review that finds least — a thorough reviewer is punished with another round.

Moving the gate to the close-out (this tick) removes most occasions for that loop to start. Fixing 80x removes the loop itself. Both are worth doing and neither replaces the other.
2026-09-20 11:37 - ticfac run epic-dha: attempt 5 reported a finding drafted for triage — proposed-tick "The moved findings gate is unreachable for a zero-commit close-out, which only the recorded no-commits rule currently makes impossible" (key 47cc30dff77bffba536f9cdf19ecad8fe2e78c5ea9cc4bc6a35d42ddeca0c125, severity low, for this repository). Triage with `ticfac finding dha 47cc30dff77bffba536f9cdf19ecad8fe2e78c5ea9cc4bc6a35d42ddeca0c125 --promote-as <tick> --by "<who>"`, `--discard --by "<who>"`, or — when it was repaired inside this epic — `--fixed-as <commit> --by "<who>"`; the tick cannot close while it is untriaged.
2026-09-20 12:21 - ticfac run epic-dha: attempt 5 merged into epic/dha as e62d101923f0; the integrated gate (go, ts) passed.
acceptance_criteria: A tick with untriaged findings closes and the run continues; the epic PR body carries every untriaged finding's full text; the close-out refuses to hand over if a filed finding is missing from the PR
